plan.melodySummary: The melody travels from the plaintive Oboe through the darker English Horn, sinks into the shadowy Cello, and re-emerges in the Tenor Sax before the Oboe returns for a fading close. The dynamic arc rises from near-silence (!pp!) to a restrained !mp! high point around mm.13-18, then dissolves back into hushed, unresolved stillness.

sections.label: Phrase A — First Statement
sections.notes: Enter alone and exposed at !pp!, dark and mysterious; let phrase ends hang unresolved. Cello sustains isolated low open fifths only under mm.3-5, otherwise silence.

sections.label: Phrase A' — Handover to Dark Reed
sections.notes: Take over in the low, veiled register at !p!, slightly warmer but still shadowy. Cello whispers a sustained fifth on the Am measures only; leave mm.9-10 nearly bare.

sections.label: Phrase B — Low Ascent to High Point
sections.notes: Carry the melody in a rich, dark tenor register, growing to !mp! — the emotional high point. English Horn adds a spare chromatic neighbor-tone line beneath at !p!; Tenor Sax gives a low sustained pedal, never louder than the Cello.

sections.label: Phrase C — Warm Return & Fade
sections.notes: Enter at !mp! then diminuendo steadily to !pp! by m.24, breathy and mysterious. Oboe returns only on the final note m.24 as a faint high shimmer; Cello sustains a low open fifth, softer than the Sax throughout.

Oboe.instruction: Open the piece alone and exposed at !pp!; play with a thin, distant tone and let phrase endings float unresolved. Tacet through the middle, returning only for a single hushed high note in m.24.

English Horn.instruction: Carry the melody in your dark low-middle register at !p!, veiled and mysterious. In mm.13-18 drop to a sparse chromatic neighbor-tone countermelody at !p!, always quieter than the Cello.

Tenor Sax.instruction: In mm.13-18 provide a low sustained pedal at !pp!, softer than the Cello melody. Take the melody in mm.19-24 at !mp! with a breathy timbre, diminishing to !pp! by the end.

Cello.instruction: For mm.1-12 and 19-24 play only isolated sustained low open fifths under Am/E7 at !pp!, leaving whole measures of silence. In mm.13-18 rise to carry the melody in the dark tenor register, swelling to !mp! as the high point.
